Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "Gulliver's Travels", "unit": 15, "heading": "CHAPTER III.", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en99-015-0008", "target": "Его величество послал за тремя великими учёными, которые тогда находились при нём на еженедельном дежурстве, согласно обычаю той страны. Эти господа, некоторое время со всей тщательностью рассматривав моё сложение, разошлись во мнениях обо мне. Все они согласились, что я не мог появиться на свет по обычным законам природы, потому что я не был устроен так, чтобы сохранять свою жизнь ни быстротой бега, ни лазаньем по деревьям, ни рытьём нор в земле. По моим зубам, которые они осмотрели с большой точностью, они заметили, что я животное плотоядное; но так как большинство четвероногих мне не по силам, а полевые мыши и некоторые другие слишком проворны, они не могли представить себе, как я мог бы прокормиться, разве что питаясь улитками и другими насекомыми, чего я, как они брались доказать многими учёными доводами, никак не мог делать. Один из этих виртуозов, казалось, думал, что я могу быть эмбрионом, или недоноском. Но это мнение отвергли двое других, заметив, что мои члены совершенны и закончены и что я прожил уже несколько лет, как явствовало из моей бороды, щетину которой они ясно разглядели через увеличительное стекло. Они не допускали, чтобы я был карликом, потому что моя малость превосходила всякое сравнение: ведь любимый карлик королевы, самый маленький из когда-либо известных в том королевстве, был почти тридцати футов ростом. После долгих прений они единогласно заключили, что я всего лишь [[I]]relplum scalcath[[/I]], что буквально переводится как [[I]]lusus naturæ[[/I]]; решение, в точности согласное с новейшей философией Европы, профессора которой, пренебрегая старой уловкой скрытых причин, посредством которой последователи Аристотеля тщетно пытались прикрыть своё невежество, изобрели это чудесное разрешение всех трудностей — к невыразимому преуспеянию человеческого знания.", "source_sha256": "800e9eb9f629e6b4f6b6dc3d20238e88dd45d02c91e533c7dd96c7e73846b806", "target_id": "ru-en99-015-0008", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "715df505ecc3f1dc2e27bbbca17edae60d2a9c5de4af077284dbdebe494094f5"}, {"source_id": "en99-015-0009", "target": "После этого решительного заключения я просил выслушать меня в нескольких словах. Я обратился к королю и заверил его величество, «что прибыл из страны, где обитают многие миллионы людей обоего пола моего роста; где животные, деревья и дома все соразмерны, и где, следовательно, я мог бы так же хорошо защищать себя и находить пропитание, как любой из подданных его величества здесь; что я почитаю полным ответом на доводы этих господ». На это они лишь ответили усмешкой презрения, сказав, «что фермер очень хорошо выучил меня моему уроку». Король, обладавший гораздо лучшим разумением, отпустил своих учёных и послал за фермером, который по счастью ещё не уехал из города. Допросив его сначала наедине, а затем сопоставив с мной и с молодой девочкой, его величество начал думать, что то, что мы ему рассказали, возможно, и правда. Он пожелал, чтобы королева распорядилась обо мне особенно заботиться; и был того мнения, что Глюмдальклич должна по-прежнему оставаться при своей должности, ходить за мной, потому что он заметил, что мы очень привязаны друг к другу. Для неё при дворе приготовили удобные покои: к ней приставили своего рода гувернантку, чтобы заботиться о её воспитании, горничную, чтобы одевать её, и двух других слуг для чёрной работы; но забота обо мне была целиком отдана ей одной. Королева повелела своему столяру-краснодеревщику смастерить ящик, который мог бы служить мне спальней, по образцу, о котором мы с Глюмдальклич условимся. Этот человек был весьма искусным мастером и по моим указаниям за три недели закончил для меня деревянную комнату шестнадцати футов в квадрате и двенадцати футов в вышину, с подъёмными окнами, дверью и двумя чуланчиками, подобную лондонской спальне. Доска, образовывавшая потолок, поднималась и опускалась на двух петлях, чтобы вкладывать постель, уже обставленную обойщиком её величества; Глюмдальклич каждый день вынимала её проветривать, собственными руками стелила её и, опуская на ночь, запирала крышу надо мной. Один искусный мастер, славившийся маленькими диковинками, взялся сделать мне два стула со спинками и рамами из вещества, не похожего на слоновую кость, и два стола с шкафчиком, чтобы класть мои вещи. Комната была обита мягкой стёжкой со всех сторон, а также пол и потолок, чтобы предупредить всякое несчастье от небрежности тех, кто будет меня носить, и ослабить силу толчка, когда я ехал в карете. Я попросил замок для моей двери, чтобы не пускать внутрь крыс и мышей. Кузнец после нескольких попыток сделал самый маленький замок из виденных ими, ибо я встречал больший на воротах дворянского дома в Англии. Я ухитрился держать ключ в своём собственном кармане, опасаясь, что Глюмдальклич его потеряет. Королева также приказала достать самые тонкие шелка, какие только можно найти, чтобы сшить мне платье, немногим толще английского одеяла, весьма стеснявшее меня, пока я к нему не привык. Платье было сшито по моде королевства, отчасти напоминавшей персидскую, отчасти китайскую, и это очень степенное и приличное одеяние.", "source_sha256": "121327f26842c466e98fd678ba54366476e03b1e2b0d97f2db3bf205868fcfb0", "target_id": "ru-en99-015-0009", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "acf1507966a976f5ee61be824abce35ec08b28360d7412ecd3a34e3687e33f2e"}], "source_language": "English", "part": 2, "book": null, "chapter": 3, "role": "PRINCIPAL_CHAPTER"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en99-015-0010", "tag": "p", "text": "The queen became so fond of my company, that she could not dine without me. I had a table placed upon the same at which her majesty ate, just at her left elbow, and a chair to sit on. Glumdalclitch stood on a stool on the floor near my table, to assist and take care of me. I had an entire set of silver dishes and plates, and other necessaries, which, in proportion to those of the queen, were not much bigger than what I have seen in a London toy-shop for the furniture of a baby-house: these my little nurse kept in her pocket in a silver box, and gave me at meals as I wanted them, always cleaning them herself. No person dined with the queen but the two princesses royal, the eldest sixteen years old, and the younger at that time thirteen and a month. Her majesty used to put a bit of meat upon one of my dishes, out of which I carved for myself, and her diversion was to see me eat in miniature: for the queen (who had indeed but a weak stomach) took up, at one mouthful, as much as a dozen English farmers could eat at a meal, which to me was for some time a very nauseous sight. She would craunch the wing of a lark, bones and all, between her teeth, although it were nine times as large as that of a full-grown turkey; and put a bit of bread into her mouth as big as two twelve-penny loaves. She drank out of a golden cup, above a hogshead at a draught. Her knives were twice as long as a scythe, set straight upon the handle. The spoons, forks, and other instruments, were all in the same proportion. I remember when Glumdalclitch carried me, out of curiosity, to see some of the tables at court, where ten or a dozen of those enormous knives and forks were lifted up together, I thought I had never till then beheld so terrible a sight.", "sha256": "f3bce650c8d66f479935c7fd60bbb2c8ece44fa62c362c16a2d9ea6efc87195f", "role": "paragraph", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[17]/p[10]", "source_html_sha256": "18f6ed8b66acd4464c292b334dd41673f8f9a8d97f11a68b0c907a7ca71af2e5", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "br_count": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": null, "source_container_role": null}, {"id": "en99-015-0011", "tag": "p", "text": "It is the custom, that every Wednesday (which, as I have observed, is their Sabbath) the king and queen, with the royal issue of both sexes, dine together in the apartment of his majesty, to whom I was now become a great favourite; and at these times, my little chair and table were placed at his left hand, before one of the salt-cellars. This prince took a pleasure in conversing with me, inquiring into the manners, religion, laws, government, and learning of Europe; wherein I gave him the best account I was able. His apprehension was so clear, and his judgment so exact, that he made very wise reflections and observations upon all I said. But I confess, that, after I had been a little too copious in talking of my own beloved country, of our trade and wars by sea and land, of our schisms in religion, and parties in the state; the prejudices of his education prevailed so far, that he could not forbear taking me up in his right hand, and stroking me gently with the other, after a hearty fit of laughing, asked me, “whether I was a whig or tory?” Then turning to his first minister, who waited behind him with a white staff, near as tall as the mainmast of the Royal Sovereign, he observed “how contemptible a thing was human grandeur, which could be mimicked by such diminutive insects as I: and yet,” says he, “I dare engage these creatures have their titles and distinctions of honour; they contrive little nests and burrows, that they call houses and cities; they make a figure in dress and equipage; they love, they fight, they dispute, they cheat, they betray!” And thus he continued on, while my colour came and went several times, with indignation, to hear our noble country, the mistress of arts and arms, the scourge of France, the arbitress of Europe, the seat of virtue, piety, honour, and truth, the pride and envy of the world, so contemptuously treated.", "sha256": "898f33e11ee827c2c3b88a02768d7c691544469a682298ef10fc13fe62b04bb5", "role": "paragraph", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[17]/p[11]", "source_html_sha256": "19efc900e8d354e95b22d9a02629552cd1e9839f6f2334d57fc5820d7da52581", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "br_count": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": null, "source_container_role": null}, {"id": "en99-015-0012", "tag": "p", "text": "But as I was not in a condition to resent injuries, so upon mature thoughts I began to doubt whether I was injured or no. For, after having been accustomed several months to the sight and converse of this people, and observed every object upon which I cast my eyes to be of proportionable magnitude, the horror I had at first conceived from their bulk and aspect was so far worn off, that if I had then beheld a company of English lords and ladies in their finery and birth-day clothes, acting their several parts in the most courtly manner of strutting, and bowing, and prating, to say the truth, I should have been strongly tempted to laugh as much at them as the king and his grandees did at me. Neither, indeed, could I forbear smiling at myself, when the queen used to place me upon her hand towards a looking-glass, by which both our persons appeared before me in full view together; and there could be nothing more ridiculous than the comparison; so that I really began to imagine myself dwindled many degrees below my usual size.", "sha256": "55191aa839209bc3c1f6b7278a4b1eed46ca6faa4e9efca85b9f762f40371349", "role": "paragraph", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[17]/p[12]", "source_html_sha256": "237887f5d50d8fcf279f7a2d93d01a906db2cfdc147eead4b4996cd3f580cc56", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "br_count": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": null, "source_container_role": null}, {"id": "en99-015-0013", "tag": "p", "text": "Nothing angered and mortified me so much as the queen’s dwarf; who being of the lowest stature that was ever in that country (for I verily think he was not full thirty feet high), became so insolent at seeing a creature so much beneath him, that he would always affect to swagger and look big as he passed by me in the queen’s antechamber, while I was standing on some table talking with the lords or ladies of the court, and he seldom failed of a smart word or two upon my littleness; against which I could only revenge myself by calling him brother, challenging him to wrestle, and such repartees as are usually in the mouths of court pages. One day, at dinner, this malicious little cub was so nettled with something I had said to him, that, raising himself upon the frame of her majesty’s chair, he took me up by the middle, as I was sitting down, not thinking any harm, and let me drop into a large silver bowl of cream, and then ran away as fast as he could. I fell over head and ears, and, if I had not been a good swimmer, it might have gone very hard with me; for Glumdalclitch in that instant happened to be at the other end of the room, and the queen was in such a fright, that she wanted presence of mind to assist me. But my little nurse ran to my relief, and took me out, after I had swallowed above a quart of cream. I was put to bed: however, I received no other damage than the loss of a suit of clothes, which was utterly spoiled. The dwarf was soundly whipt, and as a farther punishment, forced to drink up the bowl of cream into which he had thrown me: neither was he ever restored to favour; for soon after the queen bestowed him on a lady of high quality, so that I saw him no more, to my very great satisfaction; for I could not tell to what extremities such a malicious urchin might have carried his resentment.", "sha256": "1da9024c8ef9dec3d4f905725385cff5adf7f0a9de08c7f372d85a2ac5c4b33e", "role": "paragraph", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[17]/p[13]", "source_html_sha256": "300c066aaf0fb89c6e3e879940e4743ff291e118ec1f56093c1e8f7f0b2c9f43", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "br_count": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": null, "source_container_role": null}, {"id": "en99-015-0014", "tag": "p", "text": "He had before served me a scurvy trick, which set the queen a-laughing, although at the same time she was heartily vexed, and would have immediately cashiered him, if I had not been so generous as to intercede. Her majesty had taken a marrow-bone upon her plate, and, after knocking out the marrow, placed the bone again in the dish erect, as it stood before; the dwarf, watching his opportunity, while Glumdalclitch was gone to the side-board, mounted the stool that she stood on to take care of me at meals, took me up in both hands, and squeezing my legs together, wedged them into the marrow bone above my waist, where I stuck for some time, and made a very ridiculous figure. I believe it was near a minute before any one knew what was become of me; for I thought it below me to cry out. But, as princes seldom get their meat hot, my legs were not scalded, only my stockings and breeches in a sad condition. The dwarf, at my entreaty, had no other punishment than a sound whipping.", "sha256": "020c7ab039fa808dd1c12fbcef013c37c52b0dffd6837b3fd5083f78dee85572", "role": "paragraph", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[17]/p[14]", "source_html_sha256": "358c33f4c392dd4704e98aea0b633ffe8363dd214f3e6aa0375213db560cb0b7", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "br_count": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": null, "source_container_role": null}, {"id": "en99-015-0015", "tag": "p", "text": "I was frequently rallied by the queen upon account of my fearfulness; and she used to ask me whether the people of my country were as great cowards as myself? The occasion was this: the kingdom is much pestered with flies in summer; and these odious insects, each of them as big as a Dunstable lark, hardly gave me any rest while I sat at dinner, with their continual humming and buzzing about mine ears. They would sometimes alight upon my victuals, and leave their loathsome excrement, or spawn behind, which to me was very visible, though not to the natives of that country, whose large optics were not so acute as mine, in viewing smaller objects. Sometimes they would fix upon my nose, or forehead, where they stung me to the quick, smelling very offensively; and I could easily trace that viscous matter, which, our naturalists tell us, enables those creatures to walk with their feet upwards upon a ceiling. I had much ado to defend myself against these detestable animals, and could not forbear starting when they came on my face. It was the common practice of the dwarf, to catch a number of these insects in his hand, as schoolboys do among us, and let them out suddenly under my nose, on purpose to frighten me, and divert the queen. My remedy was to cut them in pieces with my knife, as they flew in the air, wherein my dexterity was much admired.", "sha256": "4c9e771fbe362ef98af99543a9655ca06a135faaa1b30730b3427f614baa0240", "role": "paragraph", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[17]/p[15]", "source_html_sha256": "15cf819a16a73d6c0149f89617c104f3aa669c0d8e679259c4f9bc04969adac2", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "br_count": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": null, "source_container_role": null}, {"id": "en99-015-0016", "tag": "p", "text": "I remember, one morning, when Glumdalclitch had set me in a box upon a window, as she usually did in fair days to give me air (for I durst not venture to let the box be hung on a nail out of the window, as we do with cages in England), after I had lifted up one of my sashes, and sat down at my table to eat a piece of sweet cake for my breakfast, above twenty wasps, allured by the smell, came flying into the room, humming louder than the drones of as many bagpipes. Some of them seized my cake, and carried it piecemeal away; others flew about my head and face, confounding me with the noise, and putting me in the utmost terror of their stings. However, I had the courage to rise and draw my hanger, and attack them in the air. I dispatched four of them, but the rest got away, and I presently shut my window. These insects were as large as partridges: I took out their stings, found them an inch and a half long, and as sharp as needles. I carefully preserved them all; and having since shown them, with some other curiosities, in several parts of Europe, upon my return to England I gave three of them to Gresham College, and kept the fourth for myself.", "sha256": "b31787e25abb351802e95b9404b28bb79338e539d889f3b265c95f55774f7348", "role": "paragraph", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[17]/p[16]", "source_html_sha256": "d9779a2ea0cd7ab2e80c7e12d861723153b6ebd767bf994fa3c809f970524a90", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "br_count": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": null, "source_container_role": null}]}
